standard_text: Reading and writing numbers up to 10 million in numerals and in words
meta_desc: Free P5 maths practice on numbers to 10 million: place value, words and numerals, the value of a digit, comparing and ordering. 100 questions, answers included.
key_big: After the millions, every group has three digits: two million, forty thousand and six is 2 040 006.

body_html:
Place value to 10 million

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. After the hundred thousands comes the millions place. 10 hundred thousands make 1 000 000 (one million), and 10 millions make 10 000 000 (ten million).

In a place value chart, M = millions, HTh = hundred thousands, TTh = ten thousands, Th = thousands, H = hundreds, T = tens and O = ones.

Place value discs show the same idea. Find the value of each group of discs, then add.

Reading numbers in words

Split the number into groups of three digits from the right. Read each group and say its name: “million”, then “thousand”. If a group is 000, skip its name.

NumeralsWords
2 040 006two million, forty thousand and six
5 000 300five million, three hundred
3 470 512three million, four hundred and seventy thousand, five hundred and twelve
10 000 000ten million

Writing numbers in numerals

After the millions, every group must have three digits. Use 0 to hold an empty place.

Words to numerals

Write two million, forty thousand and six in numerals.

two million → 2; forty thousand → 040; six → 006.

Answer: 2 040 006 (not 246 or 2 400 006)

Value of a digit

The digit is the symbol. Its value depends on its place. In 3 708 452 the digit 7 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 700 000, not 7.

Comparing and ordering

First count the digits: a 7-digit number is greater than any 6-digit number. If the numbers have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

3 060 500 ☐ 3 065 000

Millions: 3 = 3. Hundred thousands: 0 = 0. Ten thousands: 6 = 6. Thousands: 0 < 5.

Answer: 3 060 500 < 3 065 000

Big numbers in real life

About 6 000 000 people live in Singapore, and there are more than 1 000 000 HDB flats. In word problems with big numbers, draw a bar model to see what to find.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out zeros (two million, forty thousand and six → 246 or 2 400 006)Write three digits in each group: 2 | 040 | 006 → 2 040 006
Giving the digit, not its value (the 7 in 3 708 452 is 7)It is in the hundred thousands place: 700 000
Counting the discs (3 + 2 + 1 = 6)Add the values: 3 000 000 + 20 000 + 1 = 3 020 001
Saying “thousand” for a 000 group (5 000 300 → five million, three thousand)Skip the empty group: five million, three hundred
Comparing the first digits only (987 654 > 1 023 456)Count the digits first: 1 023 456 > 987 654

faq.q: What is taught in P5 whole numbers?
faq.a: Primary 5 students read and write numbers up to 10 million in numerals and in words, find the value of each digit, and compare and order big numbers. They also multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000.

faq.q: How do you write two million, forty thousand and six in numerals?
faq.a: Write 2 for the millions, 040 for the thousands and 006 for the ones: 2 040 006. Each group after the millions needs three digits, so zeros hold the empty places.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with numbers to 10 million?
faq.a: The most common mistake is leaving out zeros, such as writing 2 040 006 as 246 or 2 400 006. Another is giving the digit instead of its value: the 7 in 3 708 452 is worth 700 000.

faq.q: Is numbers to 10 million in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Reading and writing numbers up to 10 million in numerals and in words is part of Whole Numbers in the MOE 2021 Primary 5 Mathematics syllabus.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 5 243 816 the red 5 is in the millions place.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 7 395 024 the red 3 is in the hundred thousands place.

items.q: What number does the place value chart show?
items.e: Read the digits from the millions to the ones: 3, 0, 6, 0, 4, 0, 5. Keep every 0: it holds an empty place. The number is 3 060 405.

items.q: How many hundred thousands make 1 000 000?
items.e: Count in hundred thousands: 100 000, 200 000 … 1 000 000. That is 10 hundred thousands. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 3 × 1 000 000 = 3 000 000; 2 × 100 000 = 200 000. Add them: 3 200 000. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: In 4 753 218, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: In 4 753 218: millions 4, hundred thousands 7, ten thousands 5, thousands 3, hundreds 2, tens 1, ones 8. The hundred thousands digit is 7.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 4 152 708 the red 5 is in the ten thousands place.

items.q: How many thousands make 1 million?
items.e: 1 000 000 = 1000 × 1000. So 1000 thousands make 1 million.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 2 × 1 000 000 = 2 000 000; 4 × 10 000 = 40 000; 1 × 10 = 10. Add them: 2 040 010. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: What number does the place value chart show?
items.e: Read the digits from the millions to the ones: 8, 0, 0, 7, 0, 9, 0. Keep every 0: it holds an empty place. The number is 8 007 090.

items.q: In 6 029 517, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: In 6 029 517: millions 6, hundred thousands 0, ten thousands 2, thousands 9, hundreds 5, tens 1, ones 7. The ten thousands digit is 2.

items.q: How many millions make 10 000 000?
items.e: 10 000 000 = 10 × 1 000 000. Ten millions make ten million.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 9 316 485 the red 6 is in the thousands place.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 1 × 1 000 000 = 1 000 000; 3 × 1000 = 3000; 2 × 1 = 2. Add them: 1 003 002. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: What number is 3 millions, 4 hundred thousands and 5 tens?
In 3 860 742, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: In 3 860 742: millions 3, hundred thousands 8, ten thousands 6, thousands 0, hundreds 7, tens 4, ones 2. The thousands digit is 0. The 0 shows there are no thousands.

items.q: What number is 1 more than 9 999 999?
items.e: 9 999 999 + 1: every 9 becomes 0 as you rename, and a 1 goes in the ten millions place: 10 000 000. (9 999 998 is 1 less.)

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 4 × 1 000 000 = 4 000 000; 1 × 100 000 = 100 000; 3 × 100 = 300. Add them: 4 100 300. Write 0 in every empty place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: What number is 6 millions, 7 thousands and 2 hundreds?
items.e: 6 000 000 + 7000 + 200 = 6 007 200. There are no hundred thousands or ten thousands, so write 0 in those places.

items.q: What is the greatest 7-digit number?
items.e: Put the greatest digit, 9, in all 7 places: 9 999 999. 10 000 000 has 8 digits and 999 999 has only 6.

items.q: How do you write 3 000 000 in words?
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 3 | 000 | 000. Read each group with its name: 3 → three million; 000 → no thousands, so do not say “thousand”; 000 → nothing. So 3 000 000 is “three million”. 3 000 000 has six zeros after the 3.

items.q: How do you write 5 400 000 in words?
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 5 | 400 | 000. Read each group with its name: 5 → five million; 400 → four hundred thousand; 000 → nothing. So 5 400 000 is “five million, four hundred thousand”.

items.q: How do you write 2 040 006 in words?
c: two million, four thousand and six
two million, forty thousand and sixty
two million, forty thousand and six
two million, four hundred thousand and six
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 2 | 040 | 006. Read each group with its name: 2 → two million; 040 → forty thousand; 006 → six. So 2 040 006 is “two million, forty thousand and six”. The 0s hold empty places, so the 4 is in the ten thousands place.

items.q: 8 030 400 = eight million, ☐ thousand, four hundred. Which word goes in the box?
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 8 | 030 | 400. Read each group with its name: 8 → eight million; 030 → thirty thousand; 400 → four hundred. So 8 030 400 is “eight million, thirty thousand, four hundred”.

items.q: How do you write 7 000 045 in words?
c: seven million, four hundred and fifty
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 7 | 000 | 045. Read each group with its name: 7 → seven million; 000 → no thousands, so do not say “thousand”; 045 → forty-five. So 7 000 045 is “seven million and forty-five”.

items.q: How do you write 6 250 000 in words?
c: six million, two hundred and five thousand
six million, two hundred and fifty thousand
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 6 | 250 | 000. Read each group with its name: 6 → six million; 250 → two hundred and fifty thousand; 000 → nothing. So 6 250 000 is “six million, two hundred and fifty thousand”.

items.q: How do you write 4 506 000 in words?
c: four million, five hundred and sixty thousand
four million, fifty thousand, six hundred
four million, five hundred and six thousand
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 4 | 506 | 000. Read each group with its name: 4 → four million; 506 → five hundred and six thousand; 000 → nothing. So 4 506 000 is “four million, five hundred and six thousand”.

items.q: How do you write 10 000 000 in words?
items.e: 10 000 000 is 10 millions, so we say “ten million”. One million is 1 000 000 and one hundred thousand is 100 000.

items.q: 2 600 050 = two million, six hundred thousand and ☐. Which word goes in the box?
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 2 | 600 | 050. Read each group with its name: 2 → two million; 600 → six hundred thousand; 050 → fifty. So 2 600 050 is “two million, six hundred thousand and fifty”.

items.q: How do you write 1 300 090 in words?
c: one million, three hundred thousand and ninety
one million, three hundred thousand, nine hundred
one million, three hundred and ninety thousand
one million, thirty thousand and ninety
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 1 | 300 | 090. Read each group with its name: 1 → one million; 300 → three hundred thousand; 090 → ninety. So 1 300 090 is “one million, three hundred thousand and ninety”.

items.q: How do you write 8 017 300 in words?
c: eight million, seventeen thousand and thirty
eight million, seventy thousand, three hundred
eight million, seventeen thousand, three hundred
eight million, one hundred and seventy thousand, three hundred
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 8 | 017 | 300. Read each group with its name: 8 → eight million; 017 → seventeen thousand; 300 → three hundred. So 8 017 300 is “eight million, seventeen thousand, three hundred”. Seventeen is 17, not 70.

items.q: How do you write 9 205 060 in words?
c: nine million, two hundred and fifty thousand and sixty
nine million, two hundred and five thousand and sixty
nine million, two hundred and five thousand, six hundred
nine million, twenty-five thousand and sixty
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 9 | 205 | 060. Read each group with its name: 9 → nine million; 205 → two hundred and five thousand; 060 → sixty. So 9 205 060 is “nine million, two hundred and five thousand and sixty”.

items.q: Which number is read without the word “thousand”?
items.e: 5 000 300 has 000 in the thousands group, so we do not say “thousand”: five million, three hundred. The others: 5 003 000 is five million, three thousand; 5 300 000 is five million, three hundred thousand; 5 030 000 is five million, thirty thousand.

items.q: 9 004 700 = nine million, ☐ thousand, seven hundred. Which word goes in the box?
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 9 | 004 | 700. Read each group with its name: 9 → nine million; 004 → four thousand; 700 → seven hundred. So 9 004 700 is “nine million, four thousand, seven hundred”.

items.q: How do you write 3 470 512 in words?
c: three million, forty-seven thousand, five hundred and twelve
three million, four hundred and seventy thousand, five hundred and twelve
three million, four hundred and seven thousand, five hundred and twelve
three million, four hundred and seventy thousand, five hundred and twenty
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 3 | 470 | 512. Read each group with its name: 3 → three million; 470 → four hundred and seventy thousand; 512 → five hundred and twelve. So 3 470 512 is “three million, four hundred and seventy thousand, five hundred and twelve”. Twelve is 12, not 20.

items.q: How do you write 5 015 015 in words?
c: five million, fifteen thousand and fifty
five million, fifteen thousand and fifteen
five million, one hundred and fifty thousand and fifteen
five million, fifty thousand and fifteen
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 5 | 015 | 015. Read each group with its name: 5 → five million; 015 → fifteen thousand; 015 → fifteen. So 5 015 015 is “five million, fifteen thousand and fifteen”. Fifteen is 15; fifty is 50.

items.q: Chloe reads 4 060 000 as “four million and sixty”. What number did she really say?
items.e: “Four million and sixty” is 4 000 060: the 60 is in the tens place. 4 060 000 has 060 in the thousands group, so it is “four million, sixty thousand”. She left out the word “thousand”.

items.q: How do you write 6 080 708 in words?
c: six million, eighty thousand, seven hundred and eight
six million, eight hundred thousand, seven hundred and eight
six million, eighty thousand, seven hundred and eighty
six million, eight thousand, seven hundred and eight
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 6 | 080 | 708. Read each group with its name: 6 → six million; 080 → eighty thousand; 708 → seven hundred and eight. So 6 080 708 is “six million, eighty thousand, seven hundred and eight”.

items.q: How do you write 2 909 090 in words?
c: two million, nine hundred and nine thousand, nine hundred
two million, nine hundred and nine thousand and ninety
two million, ninety-nine thousand and ninety
two million, nine hundred and ninety thousand and ninety
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 2 | 909 | 090. Read each group with its name: 2 → two million; 909 → nine hundred and nine thousand; 090 → ninety. So 2 909 090 is “two million, nine hundred and nine thousand and ninety”.

items.q: How do you write 7 777 007 in words?
c: seven million, seven hundred and seventy thousand and seven
seven million, seven hundred and seventy-seven thousand and seventy
seven million, seven hundred and seven thousand and seven
seven million, seven hundred and seventy-seven thousand and seven
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 7 | 777 | 007. Read each group with its name: 7 → seven million; 777 → seven hundred and seventy-seven thousand; 007 → seven. So 7 777 007 is “seven million, seven hundred and seventy-seven thousand and seven”.

items.q: Which number is four million?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: four million → 4; no thousands → 000; nothing more → 000. So the number is 4 000 000. Four million has six zeros after the 4.

items.q: Which number is six million, two hundred thousand?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: six million → 6; two hundred thousand → 200; nothing more → 000. So the number is 6 200 000.

items.q: Which number is two million, forty thousand and six?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: two million → 2; forty thousand → 040; six → 006. So the number is 2 040 006. 246 and 2 400 006 leave out zeros that hold empty places.

items.q: Which number is 4 million and 25 thousand?
items.e: 4 million = 4 000 000. 25 thousand = 25 000. 4 000 000 + 25 000 = 4 025 000. The thousands group needs three digits: 025.

items.q: Which number is five million, three hundred and eight thousand?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: five million → 5; three hundred and eight thousand → 308; nothing more → 000. So the number is 5 308 000.

items.q: Which number is seven million and twenty-five?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: seven million → 7; no thousands → 000; twenty-five → 025. So the number is 7 000 025.

items.q: Which number is one million, nine hundred and fifty thousand?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: one million → 1; nine hundred and fifty thousand → 950; nothing more → 000. So the number is 1 950 000.

items.q: Which number is ten million?
items.e: Ten million = 10 × 1 000 000 = 10 000 000. Ten million is 10 millions: a 1, a 0 and six more zeros.

items.q: Which number is 3 millions, 2 ten thousands and 8 ones?
items.e: 3 000 000 + 20 000 + 8 = 3 020 008. Write 0 for the hundred thousands, thousands, hundreds and tens.

items.q: Which number is three million, seventy thousand, four hundred and one?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: three million → 3; seventy thousand → 070; four hundred and one → 401. So the number is 3 070 401.

items.q: Which number is eight million, eight thousand and eighty?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: eight million → 8; eight thousand → 008; eighty → 080. So the number is 8 008 080.

items.q: 6 380 000 = 6 million and ☐ thousand. What number goes in the box?
Which number is nine million, six hundred and four thousand, three hundred?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: nine million → 9; six hundred and four thousand → 604; three hundred → 300. So the number is 9 604 300.

items.q: Which number is four million, twelve thousand and nine?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: four million → 4; twelve thousand → 012; nine → 009. So the number is 4 012 009. Twelve thousand is 012 in the thousands group.

items.q: 2 070 000 = ☐ thousands. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 2 070 000 = 2070 × 1000, so it is 2070 thousands. (2 million is 2000 thousands, plus 70 thousands.)

items.q: Which number is two million, two hundred and two?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: two million → 2; no thousands → 000; two hundred and two → 202. So the number is 2 000 202. There are no thousands, so the thousands group is 000.
Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 5 millions, 0 hundred thousands, 3 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 2 ones → 5 030 402.

items.q: Which number is six million, one hundred and thirteen thousand and thirty?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: six million → 6; one hundred and thirteen thousand → 113; thirty → 030. So the number is 6 113 030.

items.q: Which number is five million, fifty thousand and fifteen?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: five million → 5; fifty thousand → 050; fifteen → 015. So the number is 5 050 015. Fifty is 50, fifteen is 15.

sets.title: Value of a digit, comparing and ordering

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 3 708 452?
items.e: The 7 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 7 hundred thousands = 700 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 700 000.

items.q: What is the value of the 4 in 5 246 913?
items.e: The 4 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 4 ten thousands = 40 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 40 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the millions place, so it is worth 4 millions = 4 000 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 4 000 000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 3 ten thousands is more than 0 ten thousands. So 5 430 000 > 5 403 000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 023 456 has 7 digits and 987 654 has only 6, so 1 023 456 is greater. A big first digit does not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: What is the value of the 6 in 9 413 680?
items.e: The 6 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 6 hundreds = 600. The digit is 6, but its value is 600.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 5 hundred thousands = 500 000. The digit is 5, but its value is 500 000.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 3 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 2 465 300 > 2 465 030. 2 465 300 is the greatest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 5 thousands is more than 0 thousands. So 3 065 000 > 3 060 500.

items.q: Put 4 530 000, 4 350 000, 4 503 000 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 4 millions. Hundred thousands: 3 < 5, so 4 350 000 is the least. 4 530 000 and 4 503 000 both have 5 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 0 < 3, so 4 503 000 < 4 530 000. Order: 4 350 000, 4 503 000, 4 530 000.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 8 351 207?
items.e: The 8 is in the millions place, so it is worth 8 millions = 8 000 000. The digit is 8, but its value is 8 000 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 2 thousands = 2000. The digit is 2, but its value is 2000.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 999 999 has only 6 digits. The other numbers have 7 digits, so 999 999 is the least, even though it starts with 9.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. Start with the millions: 8 millions is more than 7 millions. So 8 000 001 > 7 999 999.

items.q: Put 1 210 000, 1 201 000, 1 120 000 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: All have 1 million. Hundred thousands: 1 < 2, so 1 120 000 is the least. 1 210 000 and 1 201 000 both have 2 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 1 > 0, so 1 210 000 > 1 201 000. Order: 1 210 000, 1 201 000, 1 120 000.

items.q: In 4 400 000, the first 4 is worth how many times the second 4?
items.e: The first 4 is in the millions place: 4 000 000. The second 4 is in the hundred thousands place: 400 000. 4 000 000 ÷ 400 000 = 10. (3 600 000 is the difference, not how many times.)

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 1, 6, 0, 5 and 7 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the greatest digit in the millions place, then the next greatest, and so on: 8, 7, 6, 5, 3, 1, 0. The greatest number is 8 765 310.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundred thousands place: 8 hundred thousands is more than 0 hundred thousands. So 6 800 090 > 6 080 900. 6 800 090 is the greatest.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 1, 6, 0, 5 and 7 once. What is the least 7-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 7-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the least other digit first: 1. Then 0, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8: 1 035 678. (0 135 678 is just 135 678, which has only 6 digits.)

items.q: Put 9 900 000, 10 000 000, 9 090 000, 909 000 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 909 000 has only 6 digits, so it is the least. 10 000 000 has 8 digits, so it is the greatest. 9 090 000 < 9 900 000 (hundred thousands: 0 < 9). Order: 909 000, 9 090 000, 9 900 000, 10 000 000.

items.q: About six million people live in Singapore. Write six million in numerals.
items.e: Six million = 6 × 1 000 000 = 6 000 000: a 6 followed by six zeros. (600 000 is six hundred thousand.)

items.q: There are more than one million HDB flats in Singapore. Which number is more than one million?
items.e: One million is 1 000 000. Only 1 100 000 has 7 digits, so it is the only number greater than 1 000 000. 999 999 is 1 less than one million.

items.q: The arrow shows about how many people live in Singapore. What number does it point to?
items.e: From 0 to 10 000 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 000 000. The arrow is 1 space after 5 000 000: 6 000 000. (600 000 counts each space as 100 000.)

items.q: A bus company counted one million, six hundred and five thousand and forty rides paid with EZ-Link cards in one week. Write the number in numerals.
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: one million → 1; six hundred and five thousand → 605; forty → 040. So the number is 1 605 040.

items.q: A town council spent $2 608 000 to upgrade lifts in HDB blocks. How do you read the amount?
c: two million, six thousand, eight hundred dollars
two million, six hundred and eight thousand dollars
two hundred and sixty-eight thousand dollars
two million, six hundred and eighty thousand dollars
items.e: Split the number into groups of three from the right: 2 | 608 | 000. Read each group with its name: 2 → two million; 608 → six hundred and eight thousand; 000 → nothing. So 2 608 000 is “two million, six hundred and eight thousand”. So the amount is “two million, six hundred and eight thousand dollars”.

items.q: A charity raised $3 482 560 at its yearly show. What is the value of the 8 in this amount?
items.e: 3 482 560 is 3 millions, 4 hundred thousands, 8 ten thousands, 2 thousands, 5 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones. The 8 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth $80 000.

items.q: Library A has 1 245 000 books. Library B has 1 254 000 books. Which library has more books?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 5 ten thousands is more than 4 ten thousands. So 1 254 000 > 1 245 000. Library B has more books.

items.q: Jun Jie’s mystery number has 5 millions, 0 hundred thousands, 3 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 9 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones. What is his number?
items.e: Write one digit for each place, with 0 for the empty places: 5, 0, 3, 0, 9, 0, 4. That is 5 030 904.

items.q: Kumar reads a number aloud: “seven million, seven thousand and seventy”. Which number should he write?
items.e: Write every group after the millions with three digits: seven million → 7; seven thousand → 007; seventy → 070. So the number is 7 007 070.

items.q: City P has 1 085 000 people, City Q has 1 058 000 people and City R has 1 580 000 people. Which list goes from the most people to the fewest?
c: City Q, City P, City R
City P, City Q, City R
City R, City Q, City P
City R, City P, City Q
items.e: All have 1 million. Hundred thousands: 5 > 0, so City R has the most. City P and City Q both have 0 hundred thousands. Ten thousands: 8 > 5, so City P has more than City Q. Order: City R, City P, City Q.

items.q: A school building fund had $4 950 000. It then received $100 000 more. How much money is in the fund now?
items.e: Add 1 hundred thousand: 9 hundred thousands + 1 hundred thousand = 10 hundred thousands. Rename them as 1 million: 4 millions become 5 millions. 4 950 000 + 100 000 = 5 050 000. (4 050 000 forgets to add the 1 million.)

items.q: The number line shows how many dollars a charity has raised so far. How much has it raised?
items.e: From 3 000 000 to 4 000 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 100 000. The arrow is 2 spaces after 3 500 000: 3 600 000, 3 700 000. The charity has raised $3 700 000. (3 070 000 counts each space as 10 000.)

items.q: A factory makes 45 000 drink cans a day. How many cans does it make in 100 days?
items.e: 45 000 × 100: multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left. 45 000 × 100 = 4 500 000. (450 000 is × 10 and 45 000 000 is × 1000.)

items.q: A fund of $3 600 000 is shared equally among 100 schools. How much does each school get?
items.e: 3 600 000 ÷ 100: dividing by 100 moves each digit two places to the right. 3 600 000 ÷ 100 = 36 000. Each school gets $36 000. (360 000 is ÷ 10.)

items.q: Siti makes the greatest 7-digit number that has 7 different digits. What is her number?
items.e: Use the greatest digits, each only once, from the millions place down: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3. Her number is 9 876 543. (9 999 999 uses the same digit 7 times.)

items.q: A theme park had 2 500 000 visitors last year. This year it had 400 000 more visitors than last year. How many visitors did it have this year?
items.e: This year’s bar is last year’s bar plus 400 000. 2 500 000 + 400 000 = 2 900 000. (2 100 000 subtracts instead of adding.)

items.q: Book Fair A had 1 350 000 visitors. Book Fair B had 2 100 000 visitors. How many more visitors did Fair B have than Fair A?
items.e: The difference is the part marked ?. 2 100 000 − 1 350 000 = 750 000. Rename 1 million as 10 hundred thousands first. (1 250 000 takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in each place.)

items.q: A museum had 1 800 000 visitors in two years. In the 2nd year it had twice as many visitors as in the 1st year. How many visitors did it have in the 1st year?
items.e: 1st year = 1 unit, 2nd year = 2 units. 3 units = 1 800 000. 1 unit = 1 800 000 ÷ 3 = 600 000. (900 000 splits the total into 2 parts, and 1 200 000 is the 2nd year.)

items.q: A factory made 3 600 000 bottles of water in March and April. It made 400 000 more bottles in April than in March. How many bottles did it make in March?
items.e: Take away the extra 400 000: 3 600 000 − 400 000 = 3 200 000. Now the two bars are equal: 2 units = 3 200 000, so 1 unit = 1 600 000. March: 1 600 000. (2 000 000 is April.)

items.q: An online shop had 6 400 000 visits in a year. It had 4 times as many visits on its app as on its website. How many visits were on its website?
items.e: Website = 1 unit, app = 4 units. 5 units = 6 400 000. 1 unit = 6 400 000 ÷ 5 = 1 280 000. (1 600 000 divides by 4 instead of 5, and 128 000 leaves out a zero.)
